one_star_reviews.text:
I am sharing my personal experience so others seeking psychiatric care can make an informed decision before choosing Cognacity.

In short, I came here seeking a psychiatric assessment during a difficult time in my life. I found the sign-up process quite difficult, with poor communication. I was matched with Dr. Laughton. She was kind and empathetic. However, despite those qualities, my overall experience left me without confidence in the care being provided.

At the end of my first appointment, she suggested a treatment plan but asked me to return for a second session (at a further cost of £485), saying we "needed more time." In that second session, I had to repeat much of what I had already shared in the first and at the end of it, she gave me the same treatment plan she had outlined previously. It was not clear to me why a second full session had been necessary.

I was prescribed several medications, and was surprised when the pharmacist informed me that what had been called in differed from the plan we had agreed to. When I contacted the clinic, Dr. Laughton told me she had changed her mind about the medication after I had already left without attempting to contact me. In my view, significant changes to a treatment plan should be discussed directly with the patient, and this caused me to lose confidence in the care being provided.

That, along with other concerns, prompted me to contacted the operations manager for a refund of my appointment fee, so I could seek care elsewhere. Cognacity ultimately agreed to refund half of the costs. However, despite repeated assurances that the refund had been authorised, it ultimately took 31 days and multiple unanswered follow-up emails before the funds were finally returned.

I genuinely hope this feedback leads to improvements, but I could not in good conscience leave no record of my experience.

I booked my kids (5 and 11) and two nieces (9 and 10) in for a swim (and another niece to watch who had a broken arm). We were refused entry, as Karen decided when we arrived, that we were not a ‘family’ and it was ‘family bookings only’.

There is no explanation on the website of what ‘family booking’ means. I would reasonably argue, that we were in fact, a ‘family booking’. They do say no parties, but also that exceptions will be made for ‘small family parties’. Again, we met this requirement.

I know of friends who have had their kids and their kids’ friends to the pool, and the reviews both on Google and the pool website are from various groups including; grandparents and grandkids, friends meeting other friends with their kids, families including cousins… so why us? Why pick on us to say no to? My little girl was heartbroken and stood crying in the car park.

They are such well mannered girls and we had no food/inflatables with us. We’ve always looked after the pool; been clean, quiet and considerate, and have been happy to get out long before the next guests.

Even when I explained it was a birthday, Karen was wholly uncaring. I cannot imaging being faced with a child excited about a birthday and for no clear reason, ruining their day.

*update*

1. Karen is now giving a different explanation, and relying on a new rule. What does no groups of children mean please, Karen? I (an adult) brought some children, so the booking was not just a group of children? Surely, anyone bringing more than one child would be refused entry based on this new rule? Or are you picking and choosing who to apply this to?
2. No, we could not book anywhere else, it was 2:30pm. In the school holidays. Thanks for the suggestion though, Karen.
3. My money has been returned minus the booking fee, so I’m still out of pocket. And I still have a child who leaves the room tearful when anyone mentions their recent birthday.
4. I would have been happy to resolve this by email if Karen was willing to respond to my emails with an explanation, and maybe even a little apology for her random decision that my child will literally remember for the rest of her life.
5. This seems to be a new business who are still figuring things out (including their responsibilities under the consumer rights act). Karen seems to have an idealistic picture in her mind of who is suitable to use the pool, and who is not… if you don’t fit this… she won’t let you in.

I had a disappointing experience with this emergency lockout locksmith service.

We explained from the outset that the door had a split spindle lock and was not deadlocked, meaning turning the internal handle would have opened the door. The locksmith initially attempted to gain entry using a plastic sheet and then advised that drilling the lock was the only viable option. Based on this professional advice, I agreed to proceed. This was an especially stressful situation as I was with my elderly parents and we had just returned from A&E, so we urgently needed to gain access to the property and relied on the locksmith’s professional advice.

However, after drilling the lock, the door was ultimately opened using a letterbox tool to operate the internal handle — a non-destructive method which had not been attempted beforehand.

My concern is that this method was not attempted before the lock was drilled and replaced. I was charged £418.80 in total, including replacement lock and installation costs. In my view, unnecessary and costly destructive work was carried out before all reasonable non-destructive methods had been attempted.

The company later stated that drilling was required to relieve pressure/load within the mechanism. However, this explanation regarding pressure/load within the mechanism was only provided retrospectively and could not have been definitively confirmed without first attempting to operate the internal handle directly. As no attempt was made to use the letterbox method beforehand, it was never demonstrated that drilling was genuinely necessary in order to gain entry.

I raised these concerns directly with the company, but they declined to offer any refund.

In my view, the overall charge was unreasonable and disproportionate given the circumstances.

one_star_reviews.text:
Hi everyone, I had a driving instructor from Total Drive and after doing 10 hours, I honestly regret it. For me, the lessons felt way too slow and it felt like my money was just getting eaten up. There was no energy in the car and the instructor came across quite robotic. He even planned a holiday knowing I had my test date coming up.

Since switching to a new instructor (not from Total Drive), I’m actually enjoying lessons and I’ve learned much more in a shorter amount of time. As students trying to get our licences, we’re paying a lot of money for lessons for a reason. I was paying £40 an hour, which I know is standard and I don’t mind paying, but with this instructor it genuinely felt like I wasn’t getting what I paid for.

With my new instructor, you can actually see the passion, and he charges around £36–£37 an hour. That made me realise it’s not really about the hourly price — you can get a good instructor or a bad one regardless of what they charge. Paying more doesn’t automatically mean better teaching, and paying less doesn’t mean worse either.

What I’m trying to say is: don’t assume an instructor will automatically be great just because you’re paying a high price. You could end up wasting your time and money, so don’t be afraid to switch instructors if it’s not working for you.

When I first changed instructors, I kept stalling because it was a completely different car, but I got used to it quickly and I’m driving much better now.

Good luck to all learners and hope your doing amazing! 😁

Extras: Also forgot to add how the app isnt the best can be buggy at times and the app isnt fully functional for its purpose as well as the packaged hours arnt discounted (which dosent have to be but would generally be nice when you bulk buy) and there is transaction fees

Poor communication and customer service
Really became apparent after returning following issues with temporary repair on diesel primer (part broke in December 2025 during cam belt change and replacement part out of stock at the time).
Temporary repair started to fail in February 2026. The part I needed was back in stock. I booked it in for 5th March 2026. It took a week to get update informing me the needed part was now out of stock again. Agreed to proceed with another temporary repair. Poor communication and tricky to get a reply or answer to phone calls. 13 days after dropping car off (on 18th March) I got a text to say it’s ready. Ross said storage fees would apply if I didn’t collect that same afternoon – after the 13 days he had my vehicle, this seemed unreasonable. I don’t intend to return.

UPDATE AFTER ROSS'S REPLY: Ross's reply is a fabrication of events and timescales. I've uploaded screen shot from Google maps timeline and print screen of date stamped photo of mileage and fuel gauge demonstrating I dropped the car off on 5th March, not the 9th as Ross claims.

On 26th Feb I phoned Ross to book it in for 5th March after checking with Renault Parts that the part was available (they advised 2/3 day wait at the time). I asked Ross whether I should buy the part, but he said he has to buy it to ensure it’s correct.

It was only on the 12th March I got through on the phone to Ross (after no replies for a week) to find out the part was no longer in stock, and agreed to proceed with another temporary repair, Ross said he could likely do it today or tomorrow (12th or 13th).

Surprised, I verified this with Renault parts. I asked Renault Parts if there had been enquiries linked to my reg plate and they advised that a garage had phoned up a few hours earlier about the part. Had Ross made the call to buy the part as soon as I dropped the car off, it may still have been in stock.

Ross texted later on 12th asking if I wanted to go with an after-market part for £50 more than the Renault part, which i declined as i had already agreed to go with the temporary repair that morning, and had spent the day looking at new cars.

Ross claims in his reply the repair was done on 14th March. This is a Saturday. RF Autos is not open on Saturdays, according to their website (print screen attached). I was not contacted on that Saturday. After multiple follow ups, I got the ready to collect text on the 18th. To suggest it was ready sooner and that I was informed of that is totally untrue.

All Ross’s reply to my review needed was some acknowledgement of the delay and poor communication.

Update on the leak - still leaking and told leaks are not covered under warranty after 12 mths. Told sealant is not covered at all yet we don't know if sealant is the cause. They refuse to look at it sending only details of a repair company. Damp marks now on the wall and mould on roof line.all where the leak seems to be originating from.

Not given a time frame. At every stage we had to chase AGS up. But our fun didn't stop there. A date set for mid August and before we had replied it was confirmed. We were on holiday out of the country at this time but given the delays (we paid the deposit in April and we are now in mid August) we kept it. The fitters came and did a brilliant job and the conservatory looks really nice. That was the last positive experience. After two weeks we had to chase up again to ascertain when the plaster would come and finish the inside. To my amazement nothing had been scheduled and four weeks was the earliest. I quizzed as to why, knowing the anticipated end date, wasn't a plasterer scheduled and all I got was empty words of "understanding my frustrations" and "apologies". The plasterer was due 6 weeks post completion! Not once was the poor planning acknowledged or it's compound with the wholly unsatisfactory time frame given we were 5 months in from signing the dotted line.
So the day comes for the plaster who fails to show. This was great as I had been working nights shifts and waited up until 1100am. So more phone calls, more empty apologies and not a hint of anything to rectify the issue but a new date is booked at least.
The plaster arrives for two days of work and to be fair he grafted and was lovely. However at the end of the first day there were some concerns owing to a lack of prep and that he wasn't going to be skimming all the walls. This was questioned and my fears confirmed that they were only making good the new ceiling, column's and new roof line. This was not what was asked for and we even confirmed with the sales rep, the whole room will be plastered. However this was not represented in the technical drawings that you are asked to review and sign. These are architecture drawings and while I am not a moron I don't understand architect's drawing for buildings so, trusting the AGS team and that our request were to be met I signed. Do not sign until you have had them looked over. I did notice in my effort to check that white handles were stipulated. Again something not asked for as I asked for chrome. This was acknowledged but subsequently ignored and white handles have been fitted.
So, we now have a room that it half finished and according to AGS this is an acceptable state in which to leave a build. Elusive print on technical drawings aside how does anyone think that this would be an acceptable finish? I have complained but I may as well bend over take up the wrong'un when dealing with Derek as he seems deliberately ignorant of how bad this whole ordeal has been, how long its taken and that at some point, someone has blatantly lied to us. What is also laughable is the Derek told us the main wall doesn't need plastering. Look at the images and I defy anyone to disagree. This was compounded further with the plasterer acknowledging all walls need doing but he had not been requested to do them not had the time. He is booked back in for this to be done as a private job while we look to resolve the matter with AGS. They did offer to come back and fit trim to the damage parts of two walls though. Walls that need plastering, hence that token gesture was declined.

UPDATE:
As a new construction you need to have building regulations sign off. AGS told us this was a formality and not an issue. 3 months post build and more chasing we got the sign off yesterday 22nd April some 12 months later.

Update 2025:

2 years in and we have an internal leak. Externally there is drip drain opposite the leak which is seeping water. It seems water is cumulating under the gutter. I messaged AGS a week ago and guess what, not heard a thing.

We got married at St Audries Park in August 2024 and, sadly, our experience after the wedding has completely overshadowed what should have been a special occasion.

Following our wedding, a significant number of our personal belongings were not returned to us, including bespoke wedding items (custom made personalised vow books & A5 signs), gift cards and money (left in the manager’s possession), sentimental keepsakes and decorative items that had been handed over to venue staff.

We were later told that a large box of our belongings had been packed and posted back to us. However, nearly two years on, St Audries Park have still been unable to provide any evidence of this whatsoever — no tracking reference, no courier details, no dispatch confirmation, no proof of contents and no proof of delivery.

Despite repeatedly stating the items were “returned”, they have been unable to show any evidence that they were ever actually sent.

This has been the most frustrating part of the entire process. Had the venue simply accepted responsibility early on and tried to resolve matters properly, this review may have looked very different. Instead, this has involved nearly two years of chasing, repeated delays, contradictory responses and a refusal to provide any meaningful resolution.

What has been most disappointing is not just the loss of our belongings, but how poorly this has been handled since. The tone throughout has felt defensive, dismissive and focused more on avoiding responsibility than resolving the issue fairly. The board of directors have refused in person meetings and phone calls.

For a venue that markets itself as premium and specialises in weddings, we expected much better care, much better communication and much better accountability. We had to pay a £1k deposit which was very slowly returned after repeated chase calls, but the irony is it feels like we should have taken a deposit from St Audries Park for taking possession of our items in the end!

A beautiful venue in photographs, but based on our experience, be extremely cautious about leaving any personal belongings, sentimental items or anything of value in their care. We would not recommend this venue to any new couples.

one_star_reviews.text:
Registered my daughter at this clinic immediately after a dental trauma so she could be monitored and followed up appropriately. Her tooth was reintroduced at North Devon Hospital in October 2025. Six months later, she was diagnosed with active resorption (the tooth being rejected by the body), and the tooth had become mobile. I was told she would be referred through the NHS for specialist treatment.
I would like to thank the professionals at the clinic who assisted her that day and detected the problem.
My daughter was supposed to be referred to the Barnstaple Community Dental Service. However, when I spoke with the CDS practice manager, I was told the referral would likely be rejected because they do not deal with trauma cases. I sent an email to the clinic but received no response.
I then went to the clinic in person and asked to speak to someone responsible so the situation could be reviewed before the referral was made, to make sure it went to the right place. I was offered an appointment that same afternoon with a doctor who explained the whole process. During the appointment, he told us he had spoken with Exeter, and they had assured him they would look after my daughter’s case. I appreciated the explanation, although I wasn’t given much hope regarding my daughter’s tooth. I was told her referral process would be closely monitored.
Unfortunately, the two weeks that followed were different. Communication was inconsistent, and every person I spoke to gave me different information. When I tried to explain over the phone that it was unacceptable for something so delicate to be handled so carelessly, I was put on hold for a long time. I had to hang up because I was at work. Shortly afterwards, someone called my husband saying they had “zero tolerance for abuse.” I was never rude, only assertive and trying to make sense of the different information given by them. I don't agree with mistreating people.
Despite this, we were told they were doing their best and that my daughter’s case would be referred to the North Devon Hospital Maxillofacial Department. When we contacted Max Fax to check, we were told they hadn’t received anything, even though a week had passed since we were told it had been sent.
We went back to the clinic and told them Max Fax hadn’t received the referral. It was then sent, but Max Fax declined the case due to its complexity.
The clinic then said they would try to refer her to Bristol Dental Hospital, although we were told not to have much hope, as most cases were declined. But they would refer her and come back to us with updates.
At that point, I decided to stop relying on the clinic and contacted Bristol Dental Hospital directly in a desperate attempt to save my daughter’s adult tooth. We were advised to go to triage, even with the likelihood of being rejected; it was better than the hopelessness we felt. So we risked it, went to Bristol, our daughter was admitted, examined, and treatment started immediately. We were lucky someone was available to look at her that day.
Since 23 April, the clinic hasn’t contacted us once with any update about her referral — perhaps just relieved to have passed on an NHS case. I would not recommend this clinic for a child with a complex case.

one_star_reviews.text:
My dog was referred to Cave due to being diagnosed with Lymphoma. They were very quick to get in touch the next day and book my precious boy in we were so pleased. Went in for our consultation, we were advised it was stage 3/4 lymphoma and they took some bloods. Bloods came back and actually revealed it was stage 5. So that was the first unconfirmed and wrongly advised piece of information we were given. My dog was ok to go ahead with 1st dose of chemotherapy. A week later we went back and although he did have a tough time that week with side effects we went in and the oncologist told us in his words.... The cancer is dead, there is no more cancer in his bone marrow, he has probably lost weight due to the cancer cells being killed off. He then followed it up in the last sentence of, We will double check with our external lab who do more detailed analysis to confirm this. I get the results back, cancer has not been fully killed off but specialist is happy with the way things are going. A week later we go back, and he is some how riddled with cancer again. And this time a very different conversation was had. Totally floored us emotionally from one minute to be told he is cancer free, oncologist was smiling from ear to ear, and now this week complete opposite. You CANNOT so easily give this false hope to people who live their lives with their pets as part of the family, who would do anything for them, without first getting the facts correct and just guessing. One minute we are being told our vets blood machines don't work properly and theirs are much better. But isn't it strange how all of a sudden when my dog was no longer - quote 'Cancer free' that we were then told their machines are also not reliable!!!. We were advised it was ok to go ahead with third dose of chemo but this time it would be the decider as to whether they would continue if this had little change to the cancer or he was unable to tolerate it well. You can imagine the absolute shock given what we were told 7 days earlier. Given this was our last chance to help our little boy we went ahead. We were very concerned he had a temperature and had no immune system and pushed for antibiotics but were told no. We left, and under two days later my world came crumbling when he suddenly passed away. Not once were we warned that this was ever on the cards. We were given false hope twice and denied the full facts. We trusted this specialist with my whole world. Then to top it off, the lab my vets used to test the blood reported it was an extremely rare form of Plasmaoblastic Lymphoma - with only a few reported cases in the world. Our specialist rejected claims it was this as it was unheard of and requested more tests. Just as Wilson passed away further histology came back and confirmed it was indeed this rare lymphoma.
I give the 1 star for the absolutely lovely team on reception, and would advise that for all pet owners sake vets provide realistic factual advise to pet owners before giving false hope.

An appalling lack of care and service from the RAC

My 18‑year‑old daughter and her three friends (aged 17–18) broke down at Thorpe Park. They called the RAC at 6pm. No one arrived until midnight. During that time, we discovered that a patrol had been mistakenly sent to Thorpe Park Gardens—over 2.5 hours away. At no point had anyone from the RAC checked or clarified their actual location.
Little care was shown for the fact that four young women were stranded in a vast, deserted car park late at night. I phoned the RAC to explain that they were anxious and felt vulnerable, only to be dismissed with, “What are they worried about?”
When a patrol finally arrived, he immediately confirmed that the car was not drivable—something we had repeatedly told the RAC since 6pm. He also reported that the girls were vulnerable and should be prioritised for transport home. He then left. It was another hour before a taxi arrived. Two taxis refused to take the job because they didn’t want to drive to Wales. During this time, the RAC phone line did not answer our calls, leaving us extremely concerned about how the girls would get home.
The girls were told that someone was on their way to collect the car and were instructed to leave the keys with it. We understood this would be for a short time. However, when they arrived home at 3.45am, the car had still not been collected.
I was repeatedly assured that the car would be recovered before Thorpe Park reopened at 10am. It was not. I alerted the RAC that the car was parked just beyond the exit barrier and would cause an obstruction when the park opened. I also raised concerns about my vehicle being left unattended far longer than I had been told.
Throughout this ordeal, I had to call the RAC multiple times because I was not kept informed. I received contradictory information—at one point I was even told the car had already been collected, which was untrue. I was promised several times that someone from the “special intervention team” would call me. I received only a couple of inadequate text messages, and they did not respond to my replies. I was repeatedly told there was “nothing they could do.”
The car was finally collected at 12pm—42 hours later. I was not informed when it was picked up or when it was delivered to the garage.
The service has been unacceptable on so many levels. The lack of care for my daughter and her friends’ wellbeing and safety was shocking. The disregard for my concerns about my car being left unattended and obstructing an entrance for such a long period was appalling.
This has been the most frustrating and disappointing experience. I have been with the RAC for 30 years, but after this, I will not be renewing my breakdown cover.

4 hours waiting for rescue, 22 minutes on hold waiting to speak to someone, ETA another 4 to 6 hours. What has happened to the RAC? This is a complete scam. The amount I've paid must be absolutely staggering but in my hour of need, they're not there. Charlatans. My experience of Devonshires Solicitors reinforces many of the criticisms reflected in public reviews and employee feedback online. While the law firm presents itself as socially responsible and expert in housing law, I found its approach in disability-related disputes highly defensive, unprincipled, procedural, and overly aligned with protecting G15 and other  social landlords from accountability, corporately psychopathic and deliberately cruel.

For more than seven years, Devonshires client , London & Quadrant  housing trust ( L&Q) fiercely resisted providing a straightforward and entirely reasonable adjustment linked to my disabilities, which include schizophrenia, end-stage liver cirrhosis, and now terminal cancer. The adjustment was not extravagant or unreasonable. It primarily involved basic communication and procedural safeguards: no unannounced visits, clear written notice of appointments, weekday-only contact, and proper recording and sharing of these adjustments with staff and contractors so that I would not repeatedly face situations of managers and contractors just turning up unannounced on my doorstep demanding access and making legal threats without them giving me any opportunity to tidy up or plan for the visit or social interaction beforehand.

These reasonable  adjustments were eventually acknowledged and agreed ,but only after L&Q thrratened to evict me, in a written settlement  yet in practice they continued to be ignored, diluted, reframed, or treated as optional “preferences” under vague “vulnerability” or “service adjustment” - goodwill gesture-  policies rather than recognised as enforceable Equality Act rights.

I was forced to take legal action against L&Q yet despite formal admissions, Ombudsman findings, and written settlement agreements, Devonshires appeared more focused on reputational management and limiting liability no matter what than ensuring meaningful compliance or organisational learning. Serious issues involving disability, mental health, liver disease, and terminal cancer and immonucompromised status  were repeatedly handled in a detached and procedural manner that often seemed devoid of empathy or safeguarding awareness.

Particularly troubling was the continued use or attempted use of unannounced contractor visits even after case solicitor Shannon Morrison and Devonshires housing disputes lead and L&Q had been informed that I was immunocompromised and at serious risk of infection from unprepared  for contact and stress. Rather than treating this as a serious health and safety and Equality Act matter, the concerns often appeared minimised or reframed operationally. Morrison ,a real corporate psychopath has stubbornly declined  to acknowledge that I have terminal cancer and am immunocompromised and the health and safety risks and harm the continued  unannounced visits posed.

Morrison and Devonshires refuse to explain what steps their client is prepared to take in compliance with the Equality Act to ensure the reasonable adjustment agreed years ago is now provided.

My criticism is not that Devonshires defended its client robustly — solicitors are entitled to do that — but that the firm acted in a unprincipled ,unpfofessional and likely unlawful way and appears too institutionally embedded within the culture and interests of large social landlords, regulators and even SRA, glaring conflicting interests , to provide the degree of independence, balance, and ethical reflection that cases involving disabled and vulnerable tenants require.

In sectors involving enormous power imbalance between landlord and tenant, law firms should not merely legitimise defensive institutional behaviour through technical language and procedural manoeuvring. However, this discount was not included in the initial quotation dispite being told our development would qualify. When this was raised, SES Water reviewed the application and subsequently applied the discount, which resulted in delays to the quotation process.

Further errors and discrepancies were identified between the initial and revised quotations. These issues required correction, causing additional delays while the quotation was amended.

Once the quotation had been agreed and paid in full, we were promised an update, which was never received. Furthermore, all previous communications and the project application were lost within SES Water’s IT system. Fortunately, we had retained copies of all correspondence and documentation, which we then had to resend as proof of application.

The receipt issued for settling the quotation was incorrect, as it was addressed to the wrong location. We were assured that this would be corrected before the end of the financial year, as requested. However, the corrected receipt was only provided several months later, after repeated follow-ups. This caused unnecessary time expenditure and negatively impacted our accounts and tax return.

Throughout the process, our application was transferred between multiple representatives within the company. Each time we contacted SES Water to request updates, we were required to re-explain the situation, resulting in further inefficiency and delays.

The application was refused three times by the local authority, and SES Water failed to communicate this to us. During this period, thousands of pounds of our funds remained in SES Water’s account for over 12 months.

When works eventually commenced—more than 12 months after the initial application—they began prior to the required public notices and council approval. This led to significant disruption on the high street, leaving several businesses, shops, and a school without access for several days. The local authority had to intervene, as they had not granted consent for the works to begin.

As a result, I was forced to suspend my own work in order to coordinate their activity on-site, the public, access and local business access leading to a loss of earnings and time for highstreet business and myself. Additionally, large amounts of excavated material was left outside a working garage, preventing vehicle access and leaving a customer’s car stranded inside the premises for over 24 hours.

Overall, the lack of communication, repeated administrative errors, and disruption caused have resulted in a significant loss of time, disruption and personal income to myself and local community.

I had a really disappointing and frustrating experience at Flip Out Somerset. I went with my cheer teammates specifically to use the tumble track so we could safely practice, but the whole session felt really unsafe and poorly managed.

From the start, there were lots of people running straight across the tumble track area while we were trying to train. They were completely ignoring basic safety rules, which is especially dangerous when people are tumbling at speed. What made it worse is that there didn’t seem to be any staff properly supervising that area or stepping in to control what was happening.

We tried to deal with it ourselves by politely asking people to stop running across while we were using the track, just to avoid anyone getting hurt. Instead of listening, some of the same people started jumping onto the track and even cutting in front while we were mid-run, which could have easily caused a serious injury.

Then, to make things even more unfair, those same people went and complained about us. We were nearly kicked out, even though we were the ones actually trying to follow the rules and stay safe. When we explained the situation to staff, they didn’t seem interested in hearing our side properly. They said they would keep an eye on things, but within a few minutes they had walked away and nothing changed.

The rules also weren’t clearly explained or enforced, which just made everything more chaotic. If there are safety rules in place, they need to be made obvious and actually followed. Staff should be present and actively watching the tumble track area at all times, especially when it’s busy. Alternatively, the tumble track should be moved to a safer, more controlled space where people can’t just run across it.  Also kids ran below us when we tumbled

Overall, the lack of supervision and safety enforcement made it a really stressful experience. It felt like the people actually trying to use the equipment properly weren’t supported at all. I wouldn’t recommend it for anyone serious about training, as the environment just isn’t controlled or safe enough.    I will be sending to friends to put the same review to get this point across

one_star_reviews.text: If you are a mature student looking to study a course here don’t bother waste your time! The school system is a mess and the professionalism from the teachers is in the bin, they don’t know how to work with adults or talk to them either. I could go on a long rant about what has gone down at this place but I’ll leave it up to you to do your research.

Serious Concerns: Safety, Record Accuracy, and Student Treatment

Placement Safety Failure:
My second  placement, arranged by the placement coordinator was not properly set up in terms of health and safety. This was acknowledged by the Head of Course in my withdrawal meeting, yet I was still withdrawn. The placement provider also confirmed arrangements had not been finalised and told me to follow it up myself.

Data & Safeguarding Concerns:
Despite disclosing safeguarding issues, the college continued sharing information with family contacts and sending automated alerts after withdrawal, raising serious concerns about how my personal data and safety were handled.

Placement Hours Changed:
I recorded 41 hours, yet significantly fewer were reflected in official records with no explanation, despite hours determining progression.

Missing Coursework:
My coursework folder was removed on the day of my withdrawal and not returned. Another student also had difficulty retrieving theirs. This raises concerns about how student evidence is handled.

Misleading Summary:
The Assistant Principal’s written summary claimed I received “extensive support,” while omitting my placement hours, coursework progress, and participation, and ignoring the college’s own failings.

Inconsistent Behaviour Handling:
A student who made racist and homophobic remarks was not meaningfully challenged, and I was made aware that negative comments about their behaviour were removed and a removal decision was not upheld.

In contrast, I was treated more strictly and withdrawn despite raising safeguarding and mental health concerns.

Inconsistent Placement Support:
I was expected to resolve placement issues independently, even when arranged by the placement coordinator, while other students were given direct support and flexibility.
The Head of Course also admitted that another student’s placement should have counted only as enrichment, yet it was still accepted toward required hours.

Negative Framing to Placement Provider:
A placement provider questioned my reasons for moving placements in a way that suggested they had been given a negative impression of me. They also described the placement as one frequently used for “problem” students.

Intimidating Conduct in Meetings:
The Head of Course stood over me while I was seated and communicated in an intimidating manner. My withdrawal was justified with comments that I was “at an age where I can work,” dismissing my right to continue education.

Lack of SEND Support:
Despite a completed Form 8, support was minimal, delayed, and no referral for further assessment was made, and my needs were minimised.

Conclusion

These issues raise serious concerns about:
•	Placement safety
•	Record accuracy
•	Fair treatment of students
•	SEND support
•	Professional conduct

Prospective students and parents should be aware of these experiences.

I had an extremely negative and concerning experience on the Level 2 childcare course at Richmond upon Thames College, and I would strongly urge others to think carefully before enrolling. Any perceived prestige means nothing when your safety, mental health and education are at risk due to poor organisation and safeguarding failures.

I made a safeguarding disclosure on enrolment day about abuse at home in confidence, yet my concerns were not handled appropriately. My information continued to be shared with the same family member, putting me at further risk, and no welfare checks were carried out despite a clear decline in my wellbeing. When I approached another safeguarding lead later down the line, I was met with a focus on attendance rather than support.

There were also serious safeguarding concerns in relation to student safety. A situation involving another student escalated to the point where the father of that student outside of the college was able to contact my abusive uncle, which led to further harm for me. No effective measures were put in place to prevent or manage this, which was extremely concerning.

The way I was treated in meetings was deeply unprofessional and at times intimidating. I was brought into meetings without notice, leaving me unable to prepare. During one meeting, a senior staff member stood over me while I was seated, which felt uncomfortable and inappropriate. In another instance, the placement coordinator rolled her eyes at me during a video call when I was calmly raising concerns. I was also questioned by teachers about confidential discussions afterwards, which felt like a breach of trust.

There was a clear lack of fairness in how students were treated. Other students were supported, reassured, and given flexibility with placements, while I was pressured to manage everything independently and had valid placement hours blocked. Preferences and concerns raised by some students were accommodated, while mine were dismissed.

Support for students with additional needs also appeared inconsistent. Despite documented difficulties, I was not offered meaningful support, while others with formal plans received significantly more help. It felt as though support was only available if you already had an EHCP, with little effort made to assess or refer students who clearly needed it.

I also experienced issues with missing or potentially altered placement records, and another student reported having their folder taken and only returned after threatening action. This raises serious concerns about how student records are handled.

There were also repeated issues with staffing and supervision. Students, including those under 18, were at times left unsupervised for extended periods, and teachers appeared overstretched, sometimes managing multiple classes at once without adequate support. This raised further concerns about safeguarding and overall management.

After raising formal complaints internally, I was withdrawn from the course just 18 days later. I was not given proper notice, no clear evidence was presented, and the process felt rushed and unfair. This occurred shortly before key assessments, causing significant distress and uncertainty around my exams, including issues accessing the building and being questioned about identification during an exam.

More broadly, there appeared to be a pattern of vulnerable students struggling with mental health or difficult home situations not receiving adequate support, but instead being met with pressure or disciplinary responses.

Overall, this college showed serious failings in safeguarding, professionalism, and fairness. My experience left me feeling unsupported, disrespected, and ultimately pushed out rather than helped.

I was extremely disappointed with my recent experience regarding the referral process at St Giles Vets.

My dog had already been assessed by the out-of-hours service in what was a time-sensitive and urgent IVDD case, where prompt referral and specialist input are widely recognised as critical to outcomes. Despite this, I was still required to follow the practice’s internal referral process before a referral could be made. This caused unnecessary delay, additional stress, and additional expense at a point when urgent action was needed.

I also found my interaction with the vet to be abrupt and inflexible, and I did not feel that my interests or my pet’s welfare were treated with sufficient importance given the urgency of the situation. There appeared to be little recognition of the clinical seriousness of the case or the fact that my dog had already been assessed out of hours. The insistence on following the standard process risked further deterioration in my dog’s condition and delayed access to appropriate urgent care.

This ultimately resulted in me being charged £365 for the referral, as St Giles advised it was being made at my request rather than based on the clinical information already available and guidance from Cave Veterinary Specialists. This cost was avoidable and arose because the practice required an additional in-person assessment despite my dog already being seen out of hours.

When I raised these concerns with the centre manager, I was initially told the process would be reviewed. However, after I was required to present detailed supporting evidence, it was ultimately decided that no change was needed. This left me feeling that neither my interests nor my pet’s welfare were prioritised. In a situation where no one needed to lose, I was left financially disadvantaged.

As a result of this experience, I will be moving to a different veterinary practice to avoid similar bureaucracy, cost, and distress to both myself and my pet in future.

***UPDATE

Cave Veterinary Specialists have confirmed that St Giles did not submit a referral form. This explains why the inadequate “referral” resulted in a £365 cost to me, which would otherwise have been avoided had the referral been completed appropriately.

I therefore await reimbursement of this expense as a result of St Giles’ failure to submit a formal referral despite the clinical information already available and specialist guidance provided at the time.

It is also concerning that St Giles were 'unable to locate the referral form or access the relevant call' recording when reviewing my complaint, which is consistent with confirmation that a formal referral had not in fact been made.

I feel completely robbed after using Patterson Law. If you are facing a license revocation, take my advice: save your thousands of pounds and just redo your theory and practical tests from scratch. It is much faster, cheaper, and less stressful than dealing with this firm's "service."

Don't waste your time or your hard-earned money on Patterson Law. You’re paying for a "premium" service and getting a defense that misses half the facts. Avoid them at all costs.

After arranging for Aaron to come out to me to complete a stage 1 remap on my car he was a pleasant person to deal with on the day. However, just before his arrival I asked if he had a dyno that could be used to get live data from, and he said although he didnt have one he could input the data he gets back onto a graph for me to see the results.
When carrying out the remap, he did not talk me through anything, nor show me what was being done. The first go at it failed, so he told me to take it for a test drive to "see if it worked" which it had not. He then went into the engine bay to bench it. After saying it had been successful this time I took it for another test drive and could feel little difference, but it was getting incredibly late (8.30pm) and he assured me that it had been successful and that he would send me through the live data logging that he had got from the remap.
After saying that evening that applying the "data" to a graph didnt work, he then sent me through the next day a awfully done graph with incorrect inputs on data displaying the stock results higher than the stage 1 gains and with absolutely none of it making any sense!! I questioned this with him and after some very hit and miss replies and taking a long time for responses I asked for him to revert the car back to the original stock file.
I expressed my concerns as to it being a generic file, that the car was not safe to drive considering I had no idea what he had done or applied to the mapping of the car, and asked him how he got the data that he had tried to input into a graph.
His only response was that the car was safe to drive and that he would come out and revert it back. After speaking with other remapping centres, they had looked at the graph and picked up on even more problems with it, even realising that it was 89% AI generated, as well as letting me know he had no idea if the car was safe to drive or not, and that the "live data" had not been gotten at all.
I also received some very unprofessional emails through his email account from his partner, stating I was being rude for asking for it to be reverted and a full refund.

***Edited review***

I feel compelled to respond to the gross inaccuracies presented by the owner in his response to my original fair and honest review, which also highlighted some positives.

Rather than addressing polite and reasonable criticism in a professional manner, he chose to respond with personal attacks — including offensive remarks directed at my wife, who conducted herself throughout with nothing but politeness, restraint, and respect.

It is deeply disappointing to see such emotionally unintelligent behaviour, especially when a simple, measured response would have reflected far better on him.

Instead of engaging constructively, he resorted to baseless insinuations about our personal circumstances, including unfounded suggestions about financial difficulties — claims that are not only incorrect but entirely inappropriate.

We are both hardworking professionals in people-facing roles and expect, at the very least, a basic level of decency in return.

If the correct approach to customers in Plympton to respond with professionalism, courtesy, and accountability, then what we experienced was the complete opposite.

Since civility was clearly not reciprocated, it is only fair that the unfiltered truth is now shared.

Prospective customers should be aware: criticism — even when delivered politely — is not handled well here.

Unfortunately, the food let the experience down. The portion sizes were much smaller than expected, especially for the price. I don’t mind paying more for good food, but the quantity just didn’t justify the cost.

For starters, the goujons with honey dip came in a small metal basket with just four tiny pieces — more like nuggets — which looked like they came from Iceland up the road where you get twenty for £2. At £6.95, this was very overpriced.

The creamy mushrooms my wife ordered arrived on a small piece of bread that looked like its been on the mounjaro jabs (around 5 inches by 1 inches) with no more than two chopped mushrooms and a little sauce. Again, at £6.45, this was very poor value.

The mains were even worse. My Wife loves a steak pie and was really excited to see they had this as a special. The steak pie had barely any pastry as seen in the images, approximately 3 x 3 inches — it didn’t even touch the sides of the dish — and the meat was dry and chewy. The chips were undercooked, had maybe 5 minutes in the oven, and the peas were rock hard. Overall, the flavors were bland and the food didn’t taste fresh. It felt like corners had been cut both in preparation and portioning.

We had to request to only pay for the drinks and starters as we didn’t finish the mains and left them barely touched. The guy seemed rather angry and didnt seem to care that we had a poor experience.

After we set off, still hungry, we grabbed a colebook chippy which saved the evening. Their chips were definitely not undercooked and had more than 5 minutes 😉

Of 5 stars, I would give 1 star — 1 for the girl who served our drinks as she was lovely. I deduct 4 stars for the food, value for money, portion sizes, and the poor quality of the mains.

Update: Installation Completed – Ongoing Service Issues

Following my previous reviews, Gigaclear did eventually expedite the installation after escalation and the service went live.

While this was a positive step, the issues have unfortunately continued.

Since activation:
•	The connection has been unstable, with regular dropouts
•	Speeds are significantly below what was agreed (often less than a third)
•	Working from home has been directly impacted due to unreliable service

Despite raising this with support, resolution has been slow and communication inconsistent, including being cut off during support calls and the technical team contacting the wrong person.

I was previously provided with written confirmation that I could exit without penalty within the initial period if the service did not perform as expected. Based on current performance, the service is not meeting that standard.

At this stage, I am giving Gigaclear a final opportunity to resolve the stability and performance issues this week. If this is not achieved, I will be terminating the service.

This remains a consistent theme — initial failures, followed by reactive fixes, but ongoing difficulty delivering a stable and reliable service.

•	Honouring the original pricing
•	Three months’ free service
•	Written confirmation of exit without Early Termination Charges if performance is not satisfactory
•	Direct case handling to oversee installation

The proposal represents a fair commercial reset and protects me financially moving forward, although it does not fully address the historic disruption experienced over two failed attempts across two years.

I have requested written confirmation of installation safeguards and contract terms before proceeding.

If the installation is completed successfully and commitments are honoured, I will update this review accordingly.

disgraceful to charge entry to a building that should be open to all.

having a two-tier system where practicing christians are given free entry creates an ‘us and them’ divide and a feeling of an exclusionary clique. ironically it is the practicing CofE congregants that should be doing the most to foot the bill for the running of places like this as a way of encouraging others in and building communities.

this current system just creates divides, and excludes those who may not feel comfortable or confident entering a place of worship, atomising individuals, and building up barriers between people.

places like this are part of everyone’s shared heritage, and should be built on openness and inclusivity, not exclusion and discrimination based on religion.

at the very least there should be reduced/free entry for young people and those less well off.

i would wholeheartedly support a campaign to fund cathedrals from the vast coffers of the church and using public money, but to uncritically pass the responsibility onto us is offensive and poorly thought out.

this will only contribute more to dwindling church attendance. how can you expect to welcome people into the faith when the first experience of someone seeking to be inspired by its most important places of worship is to be met by a barrier to inclusion, a feeling of not being welcome, and an attitude that treats the church as a museum, a frozen relic from the past, rather than a living community with open doors.

I’m not sure whether this review applies to Orbital10 Yeovil or Allen Computer Services, because both businesses seem to be registered at the same address, so I honestly don’t know which company we spoke to.

I visited the shop on Wednesday with a MacBook that had been spilled on with a very small amount of coffee with milk. The computer was still turning on and making the startup sound, but then immediately shutting itself off. You could only see the Apple logo for about two seconds.

At the shop, we were told that the computer was completely dead, all data was lost, and can't be recovered due to the SDD being soldered onto the motherboard. As I had very important data on my laptop I specifically asked: “So there’s absolutely NOTHING that can be done to recover the data?” The response was: “No, NOTHING can be done, but you can leave the laptop with us for diagnostics for £40.00 to see if we can get it running, but it will have to be formatted, so all data will be lost nonetheless.'

We left.

I started searching online and found MacBook-repairs. I shipped the laptop the very same Wednesday (for fast track diagnostic at a cost of £50.00) and by Friday the laptop was already back with me, fully repaired, with ALL data recovered and intact. The total cost was £290.00 including fast track diagnostic, getting rid of the liquid and replacement of the lid sensor and audio jack.

Do you genuinely realise how much trouble such inaccurate and careless diagnoses can cause people? I could have just believed you and deal with the big trouble of losing the data. Do you understand how important the data on someone’s drive may be? Does any of that matter to you at all?

If you simply don’t know how to repair something, wouldn’t it be better to say so and refer customers to someone who can help, instead of telling them their request cannot be sorted? What exactly is the purpose of giving customers completely false information like this?

I understand that I should have had a proper backup, and unfortunately in this case I only had a partial one, but with all due respect, I genuinely feel misled.

I DO NOT recommend this shop.

I bought this caravan from a lady while it was at this garage for a service, which was stamped and documented by them.

After completing the purchase at the garage and leaving with the caravan, the wheel came off after only about 300–400 meters. None of the wheel nuts had broken – they had all come off. This could have caused a very serious accident.

According to the service documents provided by the garage, the wheels and the wheel bolt torque were checked and recorded at 130 Nm. However, after driving only a few hundred meters, the wheel completely detached.

I returned immediately to the garage to explain what had happened and asked the lady at reception who the manager was so I could speak with him. She was very rude and told us to leave, even though I was there with my 14-year-old child, who was very upset by the way we were spoken to.

The garage claimed that the problem was caused by the tyre, but a tyre issue cannot cause all the wheel nuts to come off and the entire wheel to detach. The only help I received was that someone assisted me in lifting the caravan with a jack and fitting the spare wheel.

When the wheel came off it also damaged the left wheel arch of the caravan, and all the repair costs caused by this incident were left for me to deal with.

I am very disappointed with both the quality of the service and the way this situation was handled. I will attach photos and the service documents showing exactly what happened.

one_star_reviews.text: The worst hospital in London
10 hours wait but not answer , not good hospital for emergency

This is a tough review to write because there are a couple of truly excellent doctors and nurses in this hospital. However my son had shared oncology treatment here for years alongside Great Ormond Street Hospital, and overall it was a horrific experience at Northwick Park.

On one occasion, a male nurse on the children’s ward falsely recorded that he had completed nightly observations when he hadn’t come in at all…
There were also older nurses who did not know how to correctly set up a IV drip via my son’s cannula, causing it to burst.
It was a very unfriendly place to be on and the ward managers constantly dismissed anything we had to say.

One oncology doctor verbally attacked us after we had spoken about our experience with a doctor at Great Ormond Street Hospital and it had gotten back to her. We brought our son in with what we believed was a serious issue, but instead of properly examining him, she argued with us and sent us home. A few days later we ended up at Great Ormond Street Hospital where he was diagnosed with a serious infection, and my then 11-month-old son needed morphine for the pain. Had she checked him properly rather than verbally attack us he would’ve been saved from the horrors of what he went on to experience.

After raising an official complaint via Pals, the matron of the children’s ward later spoke with us and said measures would be put in place. The doctor also apologised but denied any misconduct toward my son.

Our overall experience left us traumatised and really disappointed. Due to so much incompetency we ended up moving towns just to change the shared care hospital and thankfully had a much much better experience at Watford General with thier oncology team.

Today, I felt genuinely mistreated and offended inside this store.

The shop itself is lovely, and the employees have always been very kind. It is conveniently located near my workplace, and I am a frequent customer. I regularly purchase items both for myself and for the residences I manage in the area. I often stop by either to collect orders or buy something.

Today, I was selecting an item to complement another piece I had purchased a few weeks ago.

For reasons I genuinely do not understand, the lady at the register — whom I believe to be the owner, a grey-haired woman with shoulder-length hair and prescription glasses — suddenly became upset and began yelling at me in an extremely inappropriate manner, telling me to put things back in place and accusing me of making a mess in the store. In reality, I was simply choosing a product that I intended to purchase.

When I calmly expressed that I did not understand what the issue was, she once again, in a completely uncontrolled and hostile manner, asked me to leave the store and stated that I would not be allowed to purchase anything. I explained that I fully intended to pay for the item I had selected and that I had not created any disorder whatsoever. In fact, the condition of the store had not been caused by me.

After considerable discomfort, she eventually allowed me to pay for my purchase, and I left feeling deeply shocked and humiliated by the entire experience.

I did not break anything, steal anything, offend anyone, or behave disrespectfully toward anyone, yet I was treated in an entirely humiliating and unjustified manner.

As someone who has always supported this business and even recommended it to friends, I left feeling extremely disappointed.

No one is responsible for another person’s bad day. Professionalism, kindness, and respect should be maintained even during difficult moments. Kindness generates kindness, and empathy matters.

I attended this practice with my 20-year-old daughter and the experience was completely unacceptable. The dentist aggressively challenged why I was accompanying her because she is an adult. Even after we explained that she struggles in medical settings and has anxiety, he repeatedly demanded to know “why” and appeared unwilling to accept our explanation, as though he expected a “better” reason. Her prescribed medication is also clearly listed on her medical form.
Rather than showing any understanding or professionalism, the questioning continued in a confrontational and intimidating manner. I was then refused access to the treatment room, leaving my daughter visibly distressed and uncomfortable.
What upset us most was the way the dentist spoke to both of us. I would like to add that neither of us are confrontational people. Making this a more upsetting experience. My daughter was extremely upset witnessing the aggressive and dismissive way I was spoken to, and I can honestly say I have never experienced such unprofessional behaviour in a healthcare setting.
Patients should be treated with dignity, respect and compassion. Sadly, this appointment showed none of those qualities. We left feeling upset and humiliated, and we will never return to this practice.

ZERO STAR
I attended this practice recently after not visiting a dentist for 5 years due to anxiety, and unfortunately the experience made me feel extremely uncomfortable.
From the moment I arrived, the receptionist came across as hostile. When I went into the appointment room, the dentist did not greet me and immediately became confrontational about me wanting my mum in the room for support.
I explained that I have anxiety and feel more comfortable having my mum with me, but instead of handling this professionally or compassionately, he repeatedly spoke down to both of us and kept saying that I am “an adult” in a very dismissive tone. He also asked whether my mum was “a carer or just a mum,” which felt unnecessarily rude and belittling.
I understand practices may have policies, but there is a respectful way to communicate with anxious patients, and this was not it. The overall attitude and lack of empathy made me feel judged rather than supported.
I will not be returning and would not recommend this practice to anyone, to save you from meeting this horrible man.

one_star_reviews.text:
Avoid giving Tapi Exeter your hard earned money like the plague. Never in my life have I had such difficult, upsetting or long-winded customer service for a genuinely terrible quality product.

I am now well over a year into trying to get them to fix considerable install issues with my flooring and at this point I don't really expect any further reply from them, despite them promising to be back in touch with some last bits - it's been three and a half months since they last contacted me so I think it's a write off at this point.

There were materials issues with my flooring right from the get go, the fitter made some sloppy mistakes which I wasn't expecting for the price but he was very very nice and fixed most of them as we went along. But had I not been there to question things I would have come home to gaps and messy corners and it generally looking pretty DIY.

Within a week or so the threshold pieces started to fail, peeling up at the edges like I'd made them myself out of Papier mache. And there ensued a year of heartache of trying to get Tapi to fix the situation. I would call weekly, get fobbed off for days on the phone, never get a call back, call again, get fobbed off again, patiently wait again, weeks would pass. It took a whole year to get the issue fixed to a somewhat satisfactory standard, throughout which I was gaslit by the store manager into feeling terrible  personally for the poor fitter who was, for some god forsaken reason, responsible for some of the cost of fixing the issue with the thresholds - it really wasn't his fault that Tapi products are made of spit and sawdust.

It also transpired that an error in fitting has caused considerable damage to a wall, pushing a skirting board out and causing cracking along a section of a about three metres. They have, under duress, fixed the floor and reattached the edging but I wasn't offered any sort of reparations for the damage caused to my house which I now need to fix.

At one point, out of desperation I contacted head office, who were very friendly and suitably shocked with my treatment. But in the end they just passed me back to good old store manager Aiden in Exeter and straight back to the normal levels of terrible customer service we went.

This review is long enough... But I could fill a short book with the lunacy we went through. If you're looking for a quick easy new floor fitting (and why in god's name would you be looking for anything else) avoid Tapi Exeter like the plague.

Finally, they're wildly expensive against the competition so shop around. They did bring their price right down when I pointed this out, so don't accept their first quote.

one_star_reviews.text:
Unprofessional, unethical, and a direct breach of UK consumer law.
​I am writing this review as a business owner myself, and I am absolutely appalled by the lack of ethics, basic human decency, and blatant disregard for UK consumer law at this establishment.
​On Sunday 10th May, we visited to look at a VW Transporter worth £13,000. The battery was flat, so we agreed on a £500 deposit on the condition that they would replace it. On Saturday 16th May, I called the shop to check on progress. I spoke to Wayne, who explicitly admitted to me on the phone that they "had not even touched the van at all" yet.
​Due to personal reasons, our circumstances changed, and we went to the shop the very next day, Sunday 17th May, to inform them we couldn't proceed. Despite Wayne admitting less than 24 hours prior that the business had spent zero time, labor, or money preparing the vehicle, he refused to refund our £500.
​What followed was shockingly unprofessional. I was there with my wife and our 8-month-old son. Wayne didn't even have the basic courtesy or respect to offer us a seat. Instead, he stood there making tea and actively pretended he was leaving the premises just to get rid of us as quickly as possible.
​Wayne repeatedly pointed to the "non-refundable" clause on the receipt. However, under the Consumer Rights Act 2015 (Unfair Contract Terms), a business cannot simply pocket a deposit as an arbitrary penalty. UK contract law states that a trader can only retain a deposit to cover their actual, quantifiable financial losses suffered as a direct result of a cancellation. Because Wayne openly admitted on the 16th of May that absolutely zero work had been done and no parts had been purchased, their financial loss is non-existent. Retaining the full £500 is entirely unlawful.
​Furthermore, within seconds of showing me the paper, Wayne openly admitted that another customer had changed his mind overnight for personal reasons and was given a full refund. This proves that their "policy" isn't a fixed rule—it depends entirely on who they are looking at. This selective enforcement and refusal to return funds where no loss occurred breaches the Consumer Protection from Unfair Trading Regulations 2008, which prohibits misleading and unfair commercial practices.
​They saw us, realized they hadn't lost a single penny on the vehicle, and decided they could just take our money. I have emailed the owner directly to resolve this ethically and legally, but I have been completely ignored.
​If you choose to buy from this shop, please be extremely vigilant. We will now be escalating this matter formally to Trading Standards and via Money Claim Online (Small Claims Court) to recover our funds, plus court fees and interest.

Significant Barriers to Care and Disability Discrimination
​I am writing this to raise public awareness regarding the current state of care at Warwick House Medical Centre, particularly for those with complex needs or disabilities.
​For the past 6 months, I have faced a total lack of engagement from the GPs here, despite being under the Special Allocation Scheme (SAS). As a patient with a Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI), the lack of support has been devastating.
​The practice is currently creating impossible barriers to basic healthcare:
​Disability Discrimination: They have refused to accommodate my emotional support dog (a reasonable adjustment under the Equality Act 2010), making it impossible for me to attend the surgery for essential blood tests.
​Lack of Duty of Care: I was recently told by a GP that they "don't have time" for me, despite treating other patients. This is a direct breach of a doctor's clinical duty and the NHS Constitution.
​Systemic Failure: It isn't just me—my carer (who does not have a TBI) is also treated with total disregard by reception and management. I have spoken to several other patients facing similar issues with referrals and basic access.
​Unreasonable Demands: They expect a vulnerable patient to travel miles to a hospital for simple tests because they refuse to provide a safe, inclusive environment on-site.
​If you have a disability or require a GP who listens to carers, be aware that this practice is currently failing to meet basic standards of accessibility and medical ethics. I have been forced to escalate this to the Integrated Care Board (ICB) and the CQC.

I visited this clinic to remove a nevus on my scalp using a freezing pen treatment. During the consultation, I was clearly promised a strong result after the first procedure, with more than 50% reduction and eventually almost complete disappearance, leaving only a faint red mark without volume.
After the first treatment, there was no result at all. I was advised to proceed with a second session. After the second, there were slight changes, but the wound took a very long time to heal. The third treatment brought no improvement. Within two weeks, the nevus grew larger than it was before I started treatment.
At no point were the risks explained. No one mentioned the possibility of regrowth, worsening, or lack of results. Instead, I was given clear guarantees that were not met after the first, second, or third procedures.
The situation is now worse than before. The nevus has increased in size, causes discomfort, and even bleeds. I now have to seek private surgical removal, which means additional costs that could have been avoided.
I cancelled the fourth appointment because this process feels like a waste of money.
My conclusion: lack of transparency, unfulfilled promises, and no proper disclosure of risks. I do not recommend this freezing treatment.

An underwhelming kitchen that promised big ideas and outstanding design. I would not recommend this company at all. From start to finish there were many vague aspects, no version control on changes to plans, and  no detail as to how bespoke things would be achieved.

Our kitchen arrived with wine racks that we didn’t order , cheap looking to say the least, and with no plan as to where cupboards were going . Unreal to think it cost 24k and I had no plan drawing .

It was measured wrong and cupboards had to be cut down and doors reordered by the studio as it was their fault. To assist they provided a free labour day to cut the cupboards down and  put it right, but having badly executed it, it made everything worse. Cupboards were not square and every excuse was pointed back to us.

The wrong sinks were delivered and installed , and then we were not able to match the bespoke colour taps with the wastes , as they did not do the wastes in the matching colour as planned, due to a change in sink. We have had to reach a compromise on this which isn’t great. Initially we we were offered two different coloured wastes for the bowl and a half sink which was unbelievable. See pictures. They should have been black with a hint of copper , and yet one was copper and the other brass !!

The island was badly planned and major detail like the extractor had been forgotten. At our cost we had to purchase a worktop mounted extractor as the designer had not factored this in. Another forgotten detail.

Bespoke cupboards arrived flat packed and were put  together wrong by their installer, so new ones had to be ordered. Shelves were not wide enough by 5mm  , and fall down when loaded up, see photos of the brass bracket nearly falling out.

Even now there are bits missing but we’ve had enough. There is also much more to tell . No attention to detail whatsoever. £500 offered for compensation but nothing ever paid.

My overall experience offers advice to avoid this company and go elsewhere, backed up by only 7 positive reviews after 3 and a half years trading??????
